Two plausible invalidation patterns: drop_all_results in set_stock_config (mutation/config.rs:494) versus the finer drop_results_and_their_dependents used by pins (mutation/entities.rs:505-527), plus SetPostConfig's per-field `post_change_reaches_motion` gate (mutation/config.rs:515-531) that clears the simulation only when a field reaches motion. Three different invalidation philosophies sit next to each other.

Stock-level (StockConfig, job.stock) versus per-setup (SetupData at session/mod.rs:741, with its own commands such as SetSetupRotation and SetSetupPauseMessage) versus job-level non-stock (PostConfig, MachineProfile, ProjectSimulationSection::of(simulation_resolution) at save.rs). 'Project-level setting' fits any of these. Each has a different file twin: ProjectStockConfig, ProjectSetupSection, a PostConfig clone with no twin (save.rs comment UI-07), ProjectSimulationSection.

A persistence twin exists for stock (ProjectStockConfig, field-by-field) but not for post (`self.post.clone()`, single type); copying the wrong one yields either a duplicate struct or no file mapping.

Optional-field serde style: pin_part_models uses `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, while the other stock fields use #[serde(default = "default_stock_*")] helper functions or plain #[serde(default)].
